in.other_title: Human-AI: humans critiquing AI self-critiques exceed the AI's previous-stage accuracy
in.rationale: Kirchner et al. call for studying what assistance best helps humans judge large-model solutions. Wen et al. report that when humans judge Qwen2.5 recursive self-critiques, their accuracy at later stages exceeds the AI's previous-stage accuracy (e.g. 53.12% at critique, 7.03 points above the AI's 46.09%); tasks are multiple-choice and the questions were filtered by model accuracy.
in.scope: proposed ADDRESSES: what assistance helps humans judge solutions from models stronger than them, for humans judging Qwen2.5 self-critiques on math

text: The authors note they mainly studied legibility to smaller models, while legibility to humans is what ultimately matters, and call for future work to study more systematically what type of assistance better helps humans judge the validity of large-model solutions, expecting more extensive human studies to be fruitful.
title: Open question: what assistance best helps humans judge solutions from larger models?
